keyFindings.description: False ACCEPT of acceptance criterion 2, reproduced by the reviewer at code head 23f290e5 and found independently by both thermonuclear agents. The `*/` branch of `attached_comment` climbs upward accumulating every line into `pending` until one *starts with* `/*`, so the invariant it enforces is 'some `/*` exists above', not 'the `/*` I found opens the `*/` I saw'. Round 2's fix (23f290e5, `if not opened: break`) closed only the sub-case where the file holds no opener at all. Tree 1, ordinary prettier-clean TypeScript: `/* History: maxInputChars was 8000 before INFRA-42, and this block documents nothing below it. */` / `export const DISPATCH_TITLE_MAX = 200;` / `export const DISPATCH_SLUG_MAX = 80; /* a trailing note */` / `export const DISPATCH_BODY_MAX = 14500;` exits 0 with `body limit 14500 (...:4) fits the embedder's 19000 (...), and each names the other`, while the declaration carries no comment at all - the credit comes from line 1, which documents nothing. Tree 2: `/* maxInputChars */` / `const secret = 1;` / `const other = 2;` / `function f() { return 3; } /* side note */` / declaration exits 0, crediting three lines of executable code as the declaration's comment. The numeric gate is unaffected: the same tree with `DISPATCH_BODY_MAX = 99000` exits 1 with both numbers and the remedy, so no silent truncation escapes - what is lost is the pairing half, and the PR body's claim that the pairing `cannot rot unnoticed` is false while this stands. Same class as the regression the tester pinned at 0c5d413f, in a second shape. Remedy: the walk must credit comment text only - the `/*` it stops at must be the opener of the `*/` it saw, and no non-comment line may enter the block. The simplest shape that does it is one downward classification pass (is each line inside a comment?) and then the contiguous run above the declaration; thermonuclear-code-quality ran exactly that against the committed 61-assertion suite unchanged (61 passed, 0 failed) and against both trees above (refused). Pin tree 1 and tree 2 as red cases.

gradedNotFindings: A block comment whose closing line starts with `//` (`/*`, text, `// */`) is no longer credited: the `//` branch wins before the `*/` branch, the tree is refused naming the site and the remedy, and neither gofmt nor Biome writes such a closer. Fail-closed; the architect graded it and I agree. The downward-classification remedy above makes the case disappear rather than needing a rule.

The check binds the TypeScript literal, not the generated Go copies, which `bun run check:go` holds in a job main's ruleset does not require. Pre-existing, named in the script's header, and outside this issue.
